issues.description: Whole script file shoved into RPC response payload — wrong shape
issues.detail: The backend reads the compiled script off disk and stuffs the entire contents into the RPC response just so the browser can offer a 'Save As' dialog. The file is already on disk at script_path and there's presumably an extension/server route that can serve it. Doubling every compile result's payload size (and holding it in JS memory until the user clicks or dismisses) to avoid wiring a download endpoint is the wrong trade. If the script grows or someone compiles a big notebook, you've made the RPC fat for no reason. A patch that's smaller is almost always better — and a patch that does this through the existing file path would be smaller.

issues.description: No error handling around the file read; compile success now depends on a second I/O succeeding
issues.detail: open(script_path) is unguarded. If the file vanishes, perms are wrong, or it's not utf-8 decodable, compile_notebook now throws after compile_pipeline already succeeded. You've coupled a side feature (download convenience) to the success path of the main operation. At minimum wrap it, fall back to empty/None, and let the frontend hide the button. Better: don't read it here at all.

issues.description: GetAppIcon click target is an icon, not a button — bad taste and bad a11y
issues.detail: You attached onClick to an <SvgIcon> instead of wrapping it in a <button> or <IconButton> like the surrounding code presumably does. No keyboard activation, no focus ring, no role. titleAccess is not a substitute. The existing 'Done' link right above it uses an <a>; match the surrounding code's voice instead of inventing a new clickable-svg pattern.

issues.description: Filename fallback 'pipeline.kale.py' will never trigger and is misleading
issues.detail: props.compiledPath.split('/').pop() returns undefined only if compiledPath is empty, but the outer guard already requires compiledPath to be truthy. The || 'pipeline.kale.py' branch is dead code, and if it ever did fire it would lie about the filename. Drop the fallback or assert.

issues.description: Blob MIME 'text/plain' for a .py file is fine but inconsistent — pick one
issues.detail: Minor. text/plain works, text/x-python is more accurate. Not a blocker; mention only because if anyone later wires this to a 'preview' it will matter.

issues.description: compiledContent typed as string but the on-disk file could be anything
issues.detail: The TS type says string. Python read() with default encoding on a non-utf8 byte will raise on the server before it ever reaches the client, so the type is technically honest — but it means a bad-encoding script kills the whole compile RPC (see the unguarded read above). Worth noting the type is correct only because failure mode is 'crash earlier'.

review.summary: Adds a download button for the compiled .kale.py by reading the whole script on the server, returning it in the RPC payload, and Blob-downloading it in the browser. The feature works, but the shape is wrong: the file is already on disk; shipping it inline through every compile RPC bloats the payload and couples compile success to a second unguarded file read. The frontend wiring is also sloppy — onClick on a raw SvgIcon instead of an IconButton, a dead filename fallback, and a Blob type chosen by vibe. NEEDS-WORK: either expose a download endpoint that streams from script_path, or at minimum guard the read, make the icon an actual button, and drop the dead fallback. Then it lands.
